rounds.text: Rentomojo demonstrates exceptional operational efficiency, evidenced by a return on equity of 45.4% [E13] and a return on capital employed of 21.5% [E12], both of which significantly outperform their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. This performance is underpinned by aggressive growth, with compounded sales growth of 46% [E14] and compounded profit growth of 157% [E15] over the trailing twelve months. The company’s ability to generate cash is robust, as shown by a 1.66x cash conversion ratio, confirming that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash flow [E21]. Furthermore, the business benefits from a favorable sector tailwind in consumer services [E52], where the company’s growth metrics far exceed the sector medians of 18.5% for profit and 14.4% for sales [E53, E54]. Conceded: the stock trades at a high P/E of 76.5x [E1] and a P/B of 12.77x [E2], and the current ratio of 0.55x indicates that current liabilities exceed current assets [E25]. Despite these valuation and liquidity concerns, the rules-based screen assigns a 70/100 buy score, highlighting the strength of the underlying business momentum [E44].

Rentomojo’s current valuation is detached from its intrinsic value, as evidenced by a discounted cash flow analysis that suggests the stock is overvalued by 151.8% [E32, E33, E49]. The market is pricing in aggressive future growth, with the current share price implying a 22.7% earnings growth rate, significantly higher than the 10.0% base case assumption [E34]. This optimism is reflected in a P/E ratio of 83.36x and a P/B ratio of 12.33x, both of which vastly exceed their respective sector benchmarks of 22.05x and 2.17x [E6, E7]. Furthermore, the company faces liquidity concerns, as its current ratio of 0.55x indicates that current liabilities exceed current assets [E25]. While the company reported positive operating cash flow, it failed to generate free cash flow, which was negative at Rs -4 Cr in March 2026 [E22, E23]. Conceded: the company has demonstrated strong compounded sales growth of 46% and profit growth of 157% over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Despite these growth metrics, the stock’s technical position is weak, as it is currently trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E37].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow suggests overvaluation, the reverse DCF implies 22.7% earnings growth, and the price sits below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E32, E33, E34, E37, E49]. However, those backward-looking or model-driven valuation metrics ignore the company's elite fundamental momentum, which easily justifies paying a premium: compounded sales growth has reached 46% alongside an astonishing 157% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This stellar execution blows past sector benchmarks, delivering a robust ROE of 45.4% and an ROCE of 21.5%, which completely eclipses the sector median ROCE of 8.4% [E12, E13, E55]. Operating margins have also expanded dramatically by 21 percentage points over three years to hit 42%, while generating Rs 173 Cr in operating cash flow backed by a stellar 1.66x cash conversion [E17, E21, E22]. Finally, the rules-based screen awards the stock a solid 70 out of 100 with a medium-confidence BUY rating backed by broad sector tailwinds in Consumer Services [E44, E52]. Conceded: free cash flow was negative at Rs -4 Cr and the current ratio sits at 0.55x [E23, E25].

The bull relies on high growth rates [E14, E15] to justify a valuation that the evidence shows is detached from reality, as the stock trades at a P/E of 83.36x compared to a sector benchmark of 22.05x [E6]. While the bull highlights strong ROE and ROCE [E12, E13], it ignores that the company is currently failing to generate free cash flow, which was negative at Rs -4 Cr [E23]. Conceded: the company has achieved significant sales and profit growth [E14, E15]. However, this growth is being funded by increasing debt, which rose to Rs 302 Cr from Rs 234 Cr in just one year [E26]. Furthermore, the company’s liquidity is precarious, with a current ratio of 0.55x indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E25]. The market has already priced in aggressive expectations, as the reverse DCF shows the current price implies 22.7% earnings growth, far exceeding the 10% base case [E34]. Finally, the stock’s technical weakness, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, suggests that the market is already discounting the sustainability of these results [E37].
